elaine: quick heads-up 7 ran a pilot of an adaptive prefetch policy on ember-7b-int4 to see if we can get p50 gains without measurable QA loss. sketching results and next steps here.

micah: adaptive prefetch? how is that different from the earlier fixed-K runs?

elaine: instead of fixed top-K KV rows we pick K per-step from {4,8,16,32} based on model confidence proxy: top-token entropy + local logit gap. cheap compute inline. goal: keep most of quality while saving memory bw.

tess: nice. can you paste the runtime config you used so ops can repro?

elaine: ```
model: ember-7b-int4
decode: speculative
prefetch: adaptive
strategy: entropy-gap
adaptive-k: {low:4,mid:8,high:16,max:32}
thresholds: {entropy:1.5, gap:0.7}
fallback: full-window if repeat-fallback > 2
quant-backend: int4-gpu-accelerated
metrics: tok_latency_ms, per_prompt_ppl, top1_divergence
log-level: info
```

micah: good. short-run numbers?

elaine: 2k mixed traces, same node type as baseline.
- baseline (full prefetch): p50 token-lat = 90ms, p95 = 320ms
- fixed-K8: p50 = 72ms, p95 = 280ms
- adaptive (entropy-gap): p50 = 65ms, p95 = 290ms
- throughput uplift ~30% vs baseline.

tess: quality metrics? we need QA devset + summarization + a synthetic adversarial holdout.

elaine: quick checks:
- closed-book QA acc: baseline 80.1% -> adaptive 79.5% (delta -0.6%)
- summarization rougeL: 42.0 -> 41.7 (delta -0.3)
- adversarial hallucination set: baseline 1.8% false-positives -> adaptive 2.6% (delta +0.8%)

micah: hallucination uptick a bit concerning, though small absolute. do we see pattern in which prompts flip?

elaine: yes 7 long multi-hop QAs and fact-dense prompts where the entropy stayed low but gap was small. seems like the gap threshold underestimates uncertainty on some long contexts. example anomaly (shortened):

- prompt: "Given the passage on orbital mechanics, list the three conditions..."
- baseline continuation: factual list A B C
- adaptive continuation: A B <missing C> + speculative clause

tess: can we instrument per-token decisions to see K chosen per step and whether fallback triggered? also capture per-step logp deltas vs baseline.

elaine: yep. the pilot logs K distribution: 44% steps K=8, 31% K=4, 18% K=16, 7% K=32. fallback happened in ~0.9% of sequences (auto-full once triggered).

micah: propose ablation matrix: vary gap threshold and add a conservative mode for long-context prompts (force min K=16 if ctx_len>512). run 10k traces. also run same ablations on ember-13b-int4 to check scale effects.

tess: I'll wire the eval harness to capture top1 divergence, per-prompt ppl delta, and a token-level edit-distance metric vs baseline. also add a human spot-check batch for hallucination cases.

elaine: ops-bot can you schedule Dedicated node time (4xA100) for 4 hours tomorrow? want to run ember-7b and ember-13b ablations.

ops-bot: @elaine nodes reserved: dedicated-4a (4xA100) 2024-03-13T14:00Z for 4h (tag: adaptive-prefetch). :white_check_mark:

micah: rollout rule: if QA acc drops >1.0% OR adversarial FP increases >0.5% we block canary. also require token-level divergence median <0.5% for go.

tess: timeline: elaine runs ablations tonight (smaller 5k), then full 10k on dedicated tomorrow. I will run eval harness right after and produce a report with example diffs.

elaine: ack. one more note 7 cost estimate quick calc: average tokens/sec up by ~28% -> estimated infra cost drop of ~18% for same SLA on Dedicated (w/ quant kernels). will formalize after full run.

micah: perfect. if we see systematic long-context failures fallback rule is simple to implement: route long-context queries to full-prefetch or raise min-K. Tess, can you build the gating check in the canary pipeline?

tess: yes I'll add the checks to canary CI for this feature branch. will also add a fast alert if fallback rate >1% in canary.

elaine: starting runs now. will post a short summary + a few decode examples here when done.

ops-bot: job-173800: ablation set queued (ember-7b/13b adaptive-gap threshold sweep). ETA 3h.

micah: thanks team. small, iterative steps. :thumbsup:
